mainTopic: A פסח whose owner died, the three rules of דחוי, and a פסח mixed with other קרבנות
overview: This amud opens with the last line of a משנה: if a man set aside his קרבן פסח and then died, his son brings it as a שלמים, not as a פסח. The גמרא first quotes רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, who learns three rules about דחוי from the משנה's earlier case of an unfit animal set aside as a פסח. A ברייתא then adds detail. If the son was registered on the פסח, he brings it as a פסח. If not, he brings it as a שלמים on the 16th, because this ברייתא holds that נדרים ונדבות are not offered on יום טוב. The גמרא asks when the father died, and shows that both 'before חצות' and 'after חצות' seem to clash with one clause of the ברייתא. Five אמוראים answer: רבא (פסח שני), אביי (two separate cases), רב שרביא (the father was a גוסס), רב אשי (רבי שמעון's view), and רבינא (the animal was set aside after חצות). A new משנה then rules on a פסח mixed with other קרבנות. All the animals graze until blemished and are sold, and the owner pays for replacements at the value of the best animal. If the פסח was mixed with בכורות, רבי שמעון lets a group of כהנים eat them all. The discussion of this case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The owner of a פסח animal died
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if the owner of a designated פסח dies, his son cannot offer it as a פסח. He offers it as a שלמים instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone sets aside his פסח lamb and then dies, his son may not bring it after him as a פסח. He brings it as a שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. It gives a rule about a קרבן פסח whose owner died before it was offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן פסח belongs only to the people registered on it. Once the owner dies, it can no longer be offered as his פסח. The animal is still holy, though, so it is not wasted: it is brought as a שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sets aside (designates) an animal as a קרבן
The קרבן פסח lamb offering
Peace-offering
He shall bring it

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general idea: a leftover פסח that cannot be used as a פסח usually turns into a שלמים.

phrases.english: One who sets aside his Pesach offering and dies,
his son may not bring it after him
as a Pesach offering
but rather as a peace-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final clause of the משנה; opens this passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסח whose owner died is offered by his son as a שלמים, not as a פסח.

steps.title: Three lessons from the משנה, beginning with living animals
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the משנה teaches three rules. The first is that בעלי חיים נדחין: even a living animal can be permanently rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: Learn three things from this. Learn from it: living animals can be rejected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רב הונא says three rules can be learned from the משנה, and states the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ruled that a female set aside as a פסח is not offered as a שלמים. Instead it grazes until it gets a blemish, is sold, and the money goes to נדבה. So even while the animal was still alive, it was pushed off from the altar for good. That shows a living animal, not only a slaughtered one, can become דחוי.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא (start of the discussion)
Learn from it
Three
Living animals can be permanently rejected

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא's lessons are NOT about the dead-owner line you just read. They come from the משנה's earlier case: a female animal, or a two-year-old male, set aside as a פסח. That animal must be sold, and the money goes to נדבה.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Gemara: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
Learn three things from this.
Learn from it: living animals can be rejected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws general rules from the earlier clause of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בעלי חיים נדחין: a living animal can be permanently rejected from the altar.

steps.title: Rejected from the start still counts
steps.stepSummary: The second lesson is דחוי מעיקרא הוי דחוי: something that was never fit is still treated as permanently rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from it: something rejected from the very beginning counts as rejected.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives his second rule from the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A female animal was never fit to be a פסח, not even for a moment. One might think that if it was never 'pushed off,' it could simply go to the altar as a שלמים. The משנה says it cannot, so even something unfit from the very start counts as דחוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Rejected / pushed off from the altar
From the beginning
Is (counts as)

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: דָּחוּי מֵעִיקָּרָא הָוֵי דָּחוּי.
phrases.english: And learn from it: rejected from the start counts as rejected.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: דָּחוּי מֵעִיקָּרָא הָוֵי דָּחוּי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Something unfit from the outset is still considered דחוי.

steps.title: Rejection applies even to monetary holiness
steps.stepSummary: The third lesson is יש דחוי בדמים: rejection applies even where the holiness is only monetary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from it: there is rejection with regard to monetary value.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives his third and last rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A female set aside as a פסח only has קדושת דמים, meaning it is holy for its value, since it can never itself be a פסח. Still, it is rejected and cannot become a שלמים. Its money goes to נדבה instead. (רבינו חננאל explains that the rejection carries over to the money itself.)

keyTerms.meaning: Rejection applying to monetary holiness
Holiness of value only (not of the body of the animal)
Free-will offering fund

steps.whatToRemember: Three rules about דחוי: (1) a living animal can be rejected; (2) unfit from the start still counts as rejected; (3) rejection applies even to monetary holiness.

phrases.english: And learn from it: there is rejection regarding monetary value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and final lesson; closes רב הונא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יש דחוי בדמים: something with only monetary holiness can also be permanently rejected.

steps.title: A ברייתא adds detail: was the son registered?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא splits the dead-owner case. If the son was registered on the פסח, he brings it as a פסח. If not, he brings it as a שלמים on the 16th.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who sets aside his פסח etc.' תנו רבנן: one who sets aside his פסח and dies: if his son is registered with him, he brings it as a פסח. If his son is not registered with him, he brings it as a שלמים on the sixteenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the dead-owner line of the משנה and quotes a ברייתא that adds details to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule only applies when the son was not on the פסח. If he was registered with his father, the offering still has a living owner, so it stays a פסח. If he was not, it becomes a שלמים, and the ברייתא adds a timing detail: it is offered on the 16th of ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
Registered with him on the offering
On the sixteenth (of ניסן)
Etcetera (quoting the משנה)

phrases.english: 'One who sets aside his Pesach' etc.
The Rabbis taught:
One who sets aside his Pesach and dies,
if his son is registered with him
he brings it as a Pesach;
if his son is not registered with him,
he brings it as a peace-offering
on the sixteenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from רב הונא's lessons to the dead-owner clause of step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A registered son brings it as a פסח. An unregistered son brings it as a שלמים on the 16th.

steps.title: Why the 16th? No voluntary offerings on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the ברייתא allows the 16th but not the 15th. It concludes that this תנא holds נדרים ונדבות are not offered on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the sixteenth, yes; on the fifteenth, no. He holds: נדרים ונדבות are not brought on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes an inference from the ברייתא's words 'on the sixteenth' and explains the reason behind them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 15th of ניסן is יום טוב, while the 16th is חול המועד. This leftover שלמים is a voluntary offering, not one required on the festival. So waiting until the 16th shows the ברייתא holds that voluntary קרבנות may not be offered on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes / no
He holds (this is the reasoning)
Vow offerings and free-will offerings (voluntary קרבנות)
Festival day (here, the 15th of ניסן)

steps.whatToRemember: A son who was not registered brings his late father's פסח as a שלמים, but only on the 16th, because (per this ברייתא) voluntary offerings are not brought on יום טוב.

phrases.english: On the sixteenth, yes;
on the fifteenth, no.
He holds: vow and free-will offerings
are not offered on Yom Tov.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְשִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר אִין, לַחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording 'on the sixteenth' in the ברייתא of step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The תנא of the ברייתא holds that נדרים ונדבות are not offered on יום טוב.

steps.title: If the father died before midday, how can the son bring a Pesach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the father died. If it was before חצות, the son became an אונן before the time of the פסח, so he should not be able to bring it as a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: When did the father die? If you say he died before midday, how can the ברייתא say that if his son is registered with him, he brings it as a פסח? Mourning already took hold of the son from the very start!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts testing the ברייתא from Step 5 by asking exactly when the father died. It tries the first option, before midday, and shows that it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father died before חצות, the son became an אונן before the פסח obligation began. An אונן on the day of death cannot bring a קרבן. So the son should not be able to bring the animal as a פסח, but the ברייתא says he does.

keyTerms.meaning: When? A question asking for the exact time
If you say. Introduces a possible answer that the גמרא will test
Midday of the 14th of ניסן, when the time for the פסח begins
The status of a close mourner before burial. It blocks bringing קרבנות
From the start, before the obligation ever began

steps.confusionAlert: This is the first half of a two-sided question. The גמרא is not deciding yet. It shows that 'before midday' fails, and next it will show that 'after midday' also fails.

phrases.english: When did the father die?
phrases.notes: Sets up a question with two possible options.

phrases.english: If you say he died before midday,
phrases.notes: First option.

phrases.english: then 'if his son is registered with him'
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא.

phrases.english: he should bring it as a Pesach?
phrases.notes: Asked with surprise: how can that be?

phrases.english: But mourning took hold of him from the outset!
phrases.notes: He was an אונן before the פסח time began.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to the ברייתא from Step 5 and tests the timing of the father's death.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's first clause: if the son is registered, he brings it as a פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the father died before חצות, the son was an אונן before the obligation began. An אונן cannot bring a קרבן, so he cannot bring a פסח.

steps.title: If the father died after midday, how can it become a שלמים?
steps.stepSummary: The second option, that the father died after חצות, breaks the second clause. At חצות the animal was already fixed as a פסח, so it should not simply turn into a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say the father died after midday. Then how can the ברייתא say that if his son is not registered with him, he brings it as a שלמים? Midday already fixed it as a פסח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the other option, that the father died after midday. It shows that this option conflicts with the second half of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once חצות arrives while the animal is fit, it becomes fixed as a פסח. If its only owner then dies, it becomes a rejected פסח. A rejected פסח must graze until it gets a blemish, and then it is sold. It cannot be offered directly as a שלמים. So both timing options seem to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Switches to the other possibility
It fixed it, locking in the animal's status
Peace offering

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the two clauses. Step 7 attacked the first clause (registered son, פסח). This step attacks the second clause (son not registered, שלמים).

phrases.english: Rather, he died after midday.
phrases.notes: Second option.

phrases.english: then 'if his son is not registered with him'
phrases.notes: Quoting the second clause of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: he should bring it as a peace offering?
phrases.notes: Asked with surprise.

phrases.english: But midday already fixed it as a Pesach!
phrases.notes: So it is a rejected פסח and cannot become a שלמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question. Neither 'before' nor 'after' midday seems to fit the whole ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's second clause: if the son is not registered, he brings it as a שלמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After חצות the animal is fixed as a פסח. With no owner left, it is a rejected פסח that must graze, not a שלמים.

steps.title: רבא: He died before midday, and the son brings it on פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the father did die before חצות. When the ברייתא says 'bring it as a פסח,' it means as a פסח שני, after the mourning is over.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, he died before midday. And what does 'he brings it as a פסח' mean? It means as a פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the problem by choosing the first option, before midday, and reading the first clause differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem in Step 7 was that the son is an אונן on the 14th. רבא agrees, so the son does not bring the animal on the 14th. He brings it a month later on פסח שני, when he is no longer an אונן. Since the father died before חצות, the animal was never fixed as a פסח, so the second clause (שלמים) also works.

keyTerms.meaning: Really. Keeps the option that seemed rejected
The second פסח, on the 14th of אייר, for those who could not bring the first
And what does it mean? Introduces a new reading of the text

steps.whyThisMatters: רבא solves both attacks with one timing. Before חצות, nothing was fixed, so the שלמים clause works. The אנינות problem is solved by moving the פסח to פסח שני.

phrases.english: Rava said: Really, he died before midday,
phrases.notes: Goes back to the first option.

phrases.english: and what does 'he brings it as a Pesach' mean?
phrases.notes: Rereads the first clause.

phrases.english: As a Pesach on Pesach Sheni.
phrases.notes: By then the mourning is over.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לְעוֹלָם דְּמִית קוֹדֶם חֲצוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided question from Steps 7-8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the ברייתא's wording ('פסח' means פסח שני)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'bring it as a פסח' meant on the 14th, which an אונן cannot do.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means on פסח שני. The father died before חצות, so both clauses work.

steps.title: אביי: The ברייתא describes two separate cases
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the two clauses describe different times of death. After חצות with the son registered, he brings a פסח. Before חצות with the son not registered, he brings a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The ברייתא teaches two separate cases. If the father died after midday and his son is registered with him, the son brings it as a פסח. If the father died before midday and his son is not registered with him, the son brings it as a שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different answer. He says the ברייתא never meant one time of death for both clauses. Each clause has its own case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first clause the father died after חצות. The son's obligation was already fixed at midday, so he still brings the פסח. In the second clause the father died before חצות. The animal was never fixed as a פסח, so it can go straight to שלמים. Each attack from Steps 7-8 only worked because we assumed one time for both clauses.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches separate cases. Each clause of the text describes a different situation
Died

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to 'when did the father die?': רבא says before חצות, and 'פסח' means פסח שני. אביי says the two clauses are two different cases: after חצות for the פסח clause, before חצות for the שלמים clause.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not discuss the other two combinations (after חצות and not registered, or before חצות and registered). The ברייתא simply does not address them.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It teaches separate cases:
phrases.notes: Each clause is its own case.

phrases.english: If he died after midday,
phrases.notes: Case of the first clause.

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹ מְמוּנֶּה עִמּוֹ יְבִיאֶנּוּ לְשׁוּם פֶּסַח.
phrases.english: and his son is registered with him, he brings it as a Pesach.
phrases.notes: The obligation was fixed at חצות before the mourning.

phrases.english: If he died before midday,
phrases.notes: Case of the second clause.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בְּנוֹ מְמוּנֶּה עִמּוֹ יְבִיאֶנּוּ לְשׁוּם שְׁלָמִים.
phrases.english: and his son is not registered with him, he brings it as a peace offering.
phrases.notes: חצות never fixed it as a פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to the same two-sided question, different from רבא's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (לצדדין): each clause refers to a different time of death
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed both clauses describe one time of death, so one clause always failed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסח clause is after חצות, and the שלמים clause is before חצות. Both clauses work.

steps.title: רב שרביא: the father was dying at midday
steps.stepSummary: רב שרביא keeps the case as a death after חצות. He adds that the father was already a גוסס at חצות, so חצות never firmly locked the animal in as a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שרביא said: Really, the father died after midday. But this is a case where the father was already a גוסס at midday.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שרביא gives a new answer to the problem from Step 8. He agrees the father died after חצות, and he describes a special situation that removes the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difficulty was that at חצות the animal should already have been fixed as a פסח, so it could not later turn into a שלמים. רב שרביא says the father was a גוסס at חצות, and most people in that state die. So at חצות the animal's only owner was already treated as if he were about to die, and the animal was never firmly fixed as a פסח. That is why it can become a שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually. Used to hold on to one side of an earlier question.
A person on his deathbed, in the final moments before death.
Midday on ערב פסח, the time the פסח obligation begins.

phrases.english: Rav Sherevya said:
Really, he died after midday,
phrases.notes: He accepts the second option from Step 8.

phrases.english: and it is a case where his father was on his deathbed at midday.
phrases.notes: Since death was already expected at midday, midday did not lock in the animal as a פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer, alongside רבא and אביי, to the קשיא of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a special situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A death after חצות means the animal was already fixed as a פסח and should be permanently pushed off.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the father was a גוסס at חצות, the animal was never firmly fixed as a פסח, so it can become a שלמים.

steps.title: רב אשי: the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי also keeps the death after חצות. He explains that the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who holds that a living animal cannot be permanently pushed off.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Really, the father died after midday, and this ברייתא follows רבי שמעון. He said that living animals are not permanently pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives another answer to Step 8. He solves it by saying which תנא the ברייתא follows, not by changing the facts of the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem assumed that once the animal was rejected as a פסח, it stays rejected forever (דחוי). רבי שמעון holds that as long as an animal is still alive, it is not permanently rejected. So even after חצות, the living animal can still change its status and be brought as a שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Living animals, meaning animals not yet slaughtered.
Are permanently pushed off or rejected from being offered.
The תנא whose opinion רב אשי says the ברייתא follows.

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying the animal was never a פסח. He is saying that even if it was set aside and then disqualified, a living animal does not stay rejected forever according to רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Really, he died after midday,
and it follows Rabbi Shimon, who said:
living animals are not permanently rejected.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם דְּמִית לְאַחַר חֲצוֹת, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to Step 8. This one works by naming the תנא behind the ברייתא instead of narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a specific תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once חצות passed and the animal was disqualified as a פסח, it stays rejected forever.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי שמעון, a living animal is not permanently rejected, so it can still become a שלמים.

steps.title: רבינא: the animal was set aside after midday
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the animal was set aside after חצות and the owner died after חצות. Since only חצות fixes the status, and the animal did not exist as a פסח at חצות, it was never fixed and never rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: This is a case where he set the animal aside after midday, and the owner died after midday. This תנא holds that midday is what fixes the status.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives the last answer to Step 8. He changes when the animal was set aside, so the moment of חצות passed before it was ever a פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This תנא holds that חצות is the moment that fixes an animal as a פסח. If the animal was only designated after חצות, that moment had already passed, so it never became firmly a פסח. When the owner then died, nothing had been locked in, so it can simply be brought as a שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: He set it aside, designating the animal for a קרבן.
The owners of the קרבן.
Fixes or determines the status.

steps.whatToRemember: Five answers to the two-sided question of Steps 7-8. רבא says the father died before חצות, and 'פסח' means פסח שני. אביי says the two clauses describe two different times of death. The last three keep the death after חצות and explain why the שלמים clause still works: רב שרביא says the father was a גוסס at חצות, רב אשי says the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, and רבינא says the animal was set aside after חצות.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
It is a case where he set it aside after midday
and the owners died after midday,
and he holds that midday is what fixes the status.
phrases.notes: Since the animal was not yet designated at midday, midday never fixed it as a פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final answer to Step 8, which closes this section of the סוגיא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) by changing when the animal was designated
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every animal meant for the פסח is fixed at חצות and would be rejected if the owner died afterward.
steps.terutzMaskana: An animal designated after חצות was never fixed as a פסח, so it is not rejected and can become a שלמים.

steps.title: New משנה: a פסח mixed with other offerings
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules on a פסח that got mixed with other קרבנות. All the animals graze until they get a blemish and are sold. He then buys one animal of each type at the price of the most expensive animal and pays the difference himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a פסח got mixed up with other offerings, all of them graze until they get a blemish. Then they are sold. With money equal to the best animal among them, he brings one of this type, and with money equal to the best animal among them, he brings one of that type. He pays the extra from his own pocket.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic. It explains what to do when a פסח cannot be told apart from other קרבנות it got mixed with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot offer any of the animals, because we do not know which is the פסח and which is the other קרבן. So all of them wait until they get a blemish, which lets them be sold. Since we do not know which animal held which holiness, each type must be replaced at the value of the most expensive animal. That way no קרבן is shortchanged, and the owner covers the extra cost.

keyTerms.meaning: Got mixed up, so the animals can no longer be told apart.
Animal offerings, here other קרבנות such as אשם or עולה.
They graze until they become unfit by getting a blemish.
From his own house, meaning out of his own money.

steps.confusionAlert: He does not buy each replacement at its own animal's value. Each type of קרבן is replaced at the price of the single most valuable animal in the group, because we do not know which animal was which.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A Paschal lamb that was mixed with other offerings:
all of them graze until they get a blemish and become unfit,

phrases.aramaic: וְיִמָּכְרוּ, וְיָבִיא בִּדְמֵי הַיָּפֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן מִמִּין זֶה
phrases.english: and they are sold, and with the value of the best of them he brings one of this type,
and with the value of the best of them he brings one of that type,
and he loses the extra from his own pocket.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה that starts a new topic after the previous סוגיא ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a פסח is mixed with other קרבנות, all graze until blemished and are sold. One animal of each type is bought at the price of the most valuable animal, and the owner pays the difference.

steps.title: A פסח mixed with בכורות can be eaten by a group of כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds a new mixing case. If a פסח got mixed with בכורות, רבי שמעון rules that a חבורה made up of כהנים may eat all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסח got mixed up with firstborn animals, רבי שמעון says: if it is a group of כהנים, they may eat them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of mix-ups and gives a new case: a פסח mixed with בכורות. רבי שמעון says a group of כהנים does not need to wait for a blemish. They may simply eat the animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last case (Step 14), the mixed animals had to graze until they got a blemish, because nobody could tell which animal was which. Here there is an easy fix. A בכור is offered the same way as a פסח, and כהנים may eat both. So the כהנים offer each animal on the condition that the פסח is the פסח and the בכור is the בכור, and then they eat all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Got mixed up. Here it means the פסח can no longer be told apart from the other animals.
Firstborn male animals. They are offered as קרבנות and their meat is given to the כהנים.
A group of כהנים who registered together on one פסח.
They may eat (all the mixed animals).

steps.confusionAlert: This solution works only when the group is made up of כהנים. A non-כהן may not eat the meat of a בכור at all, so a regular group could not use this solution.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's coming discussion. Eating a בכור under the stricter rules of a פסח (only that night) cuts short the time the בכור could normally be eaten. That raises the question of whether you may knowingly shorten the eating time of a קרבן.

phrases.english: If it (the Pesach) got mixed up with firstborn animals,
phrases.notes: A new case in the list of mix-ups that started in Step 14.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
If it is a group of priests, they may eat them.
phrases.notes: Priests may eat a firstborn, and its blood service is the same as a Pesach's. So all the animals can be offered with a condition and eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from Step 14 with a new kind of mix-up. This case can be solved more easily than the earlier one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, if a פסח is mixed with בכורות and the owners are a group of כהנים, they may offer and eat all the animals.
